sol.about: The catalogued Solar System: the Sun, the planets, the Moon and the large moons, Ceres, Pluto and Charon, and the belts and the Oort cloud, as measured. Built by scripts/build-base-sol.py; every value names its source. Body facts, not the master data sheet's reference objects.

regions.name: Main asteroid belt
regions.note: edges at the 4:1 and 2:1 mean-motion resonances with Jupiter (the outer Kirkwood gaps), worked out from Jupiter's semi-major axis by Kepler's third law, a = a_J (p/q)^(2/3)

regions.name: Kuiper belt
regions.note: inner edge at Neptune's orbit (convention, from nssdca-neptune); outer edge of the classical belt at 50 AU

regions.name: Oort cloud
regions.note: outer limit set by the Galactic tide at 1 to 2 × 10^5 au (quoted); the inner edge near 5,000 au for bodies scattered by Uranus and Neptune was read in paraphrase, not quoted. A sphere (ruling).

regions.name: Saturn's D ring
regions.note: optical depth printed as 10-5; no albedo printed

regions.name: Saturn's C ring
regions.note: albedo 0.12 to 0.30 at the inner edge, 0.2 at the outer; thickness 5 m

regions.name: Cassini Division
regions.note: edges taken as the B ring's outer and the A ring's inner edge (the sheet prints no radius on this row); thickness 20 m

regions.name: Jupiter's main ring
regions.note: albedo printed as ~0.015; thickness under about 100 km

regions.name: Uranus's epsilon ring
regions.note: radius 51,149 km, width 20 to 96 km (eccentric, e = 0.0079): drawn at the middle width, 58 km; albedo printed as ~18 x 10-3

regions.name: Neptune's Le Verrier ring
regions.note: radius ~53,200 km, width printed as under 100 km: drawn at 100 km, an upper bound; albedo ~15 x 10-3

regions.name: Neptune's Adams ring
regions.note: radius 62,933 km, width ~15 km; its arcs (Courage, Liberte, Egalite, Fraternite) reach optical depth 0.12; albedo ~15 x 10-3
